overview:
If this is your first time in Morocco, a desert trip raises many questions. How long are the drives? Is the camp comfortable? What do I pack? How much should I tip? This private five-day loop from Marrakech answers them day by day, at a pace designed for first-timers: no day starts before breakfast except for the sunrise, the longest drives are broken up by stops, and every night is in a comfortable room or a desert tent with a real bed.

You cross the High Atlas to Ait Ben Haddou, follow the Road of a Thousand Kasbahs through Ouarzazate, Skoura and the Dades Valley, walk in the Todra Gorge, spend a night near the dunes in Erfoud, ride a camel into the Erg Chebbi for sunset, sleep in a desert camp, and return to Marrakech by a different road through Rissani and the black desert of Alnif.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: 5 days, 4 nights
• Start and finish: your riad or hotel in Marrakech (airport pick-up on request)
• Type: private tour with your own driver; local guide in Ait Ben Haddou
• Activity level: easy (short walks, a 1–1.5 hour camel ride)
• Nights: Ait Ben Haddou, Dades Valley, Erfoud, desert camp in Erg Chebbi
• Meals: breakfast and dinner every day

THE ROUTE DAY BY DAY
• Day 1 – Marrakech to Ait Ben Haddou: about 190 km, 4 hours with stops.
• Day 2 – Ouarzazate, Skoura and the Dades Valley: about 150 km, 3 hours.
• Day 3 – Todra Gorge and Erfoud: about 200 km, 3–4 hours.
• Day 4 – Merzouga, camel trek and desert camp: about 60 km.
• Day 5 – Back to Marrakech via Rissani and Alnif: about 560 km, 9–10 hours with stops.

WHY THIS ITINERARY WORKS FOR A FIRST TRIP
Shorter days at the start let you settle in; the night in Erfoud means you reach the dunes fresh, in the afternoon, instead of after a long drive; and the return by Rissani and Alnif shows you a different landscape rather than the same road twice.

FIRST-TIMER TIPS
• Packing: layers (desert nights can drop near 0 °C in winter), a scarf, sunglasses, sunscreen, a head torch, a small overnight bag for the camp.
• Money: carry dirhams; cards are rarely accepted outside cities.
• Tipping: customary for drivers, guides and camel handlers; your driver will advise.
• Photos: ask before photographing people.
• Clothing: modest dress is appreciated in villages.
• Food: tell us about allergies or dietary needs; hotels and camps adapt the dinners.

WHO MIGHT PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
For a slower pace, choose the [slow-paced 5-day Sahara tour](/en-US/morocco/marrakech/tours/marrakech-sahara-5-day-private-tour-slow-paced-route-through-kasbahs-oases-gorges/516c0a4377e175f37b8b31d2).

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Ask us anything before you go; we answer within a day. Tell us your room preference (double, twin, triple or family) when you book.
descriptions:
What to expect: about 4 hours of driving over a mountain road with many bends, a guided walk through a UNESCO kasbah village and a quiet evening.

Your driver picks you up at your riad or hotel after breakfast and heads south across the Haouz plain towards the High Atlas. The road climbs through walnut groves and Berber villages of red earth; a good first stop is Taddert, where a women's argan cooperative shows how the oil is cracked, roasted and pressed by hand. Higher up, the Tizi n'Tichka pass (about 2,260 m) is the highest paved pass in Morocco, with wide views over the mountains, snow-capped in winter.

On the southern side the landscape turns dry and mineral. You reach Ait Ben Haddou in the early afternoon, have lunch in the village, then a local guide walks you across the river and up through the ksar, a fortified village of earthen houses listed by UNESCO and used in films such as Gladiator. The climb to the old granary at the top takes about 40 minutes and gives the best view over the Ounila valley. Stay for the late-afternoon light, when the walls turn orange, then check in to your hotel for dinner.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
09:00 – Pick-up in Marrakech.
10:30 – Argan cooperative in the foothills (optional).
11:30 – Tizi n'Tichka pass (photo stop).
14:00 – Ait Ben Haddou; lunch (not included).
16:30 – Guided walk through the ksar.
19:30 – Dinner at your hotel.

FIRST-TIMER TIPS
• Take car-sickness medication before the pass if needed; sit in front if you can.
• Bring a warm layer: the pass is often 10 °C cooler than Marrakech.
• Wear shoes with grip for the steps of the ksar.

INCLUDED: vehicle and driver, local guide in Ait Ben Haddou, hotel with dinner and breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, drinks, tips.

Overnight: Ait Ben Haddou (hotel)
Meals: dinner

What to expect: short drives and several stops along the Road of a Thousand Kasbahs.

If you're an early riser, walk back to the ksar for sunrise, when it's empty and quiet. After breakfast, drive 30 minutes to Ouarzazate, the 'Hollywood of the desert'. Visit the Taourirt Kasbah, the earthen palace of the Glaoui family with its maze of rooms and painted ceilings, or one of the film studios on the edge of town, where sets from films shot in the region still stand.

Then follow the oases east. In Skoura, stop at a viewpoint over the palm grove and the Amridil Kasbah, one of the best-preserved in the south and the one pictured on the old 50-dirham note. After lunch, drive through Kelaat M'Gouna and the Valley of Roses, where hedges of Damask roses line the fields and small shops sell rose water and rose oil. In the late afternoon you enter the Dades Valley; if the light is good, your driver can take you up the hairpin bends of the Dades gorge for a view from above, before dinner at your hotel in the valley.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
08:00 – Optional sunrise walk at the ksar; breakfast.
09:30 – Ouarzazate: Taourirt Kasbah or film studios (1–1.5 hours).
12:00 – Skoura palm grove and Amridil Kasbah viewpoint.
13:00 – Lunch (not included).
14:30 – Kelaat M'Gouna and the Valley of Roses.
16:30 – Dades Valley hotel.

FIRST-TIMER TIPS
• Shops may offer you tea; it is hospitality, and buying is never required.
• Rose products vary in quality; the cooperatives usually sell the real thing.
• Keep small change for entrance fees.

INCLUDED: vehicle and driver, hotel with dinner and breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: entrance fees, lunch, tips.

Overnight: Dades Valley (hotel)
Meals: breakfast and dinner

What to expect: a flat walk in a canyon, fossil workshops and an easy afternoon close to the desert.

In the morning drive past the rock formations of the Dades, nicknamed 'monkey fingers', to Tinghir, where a viewpoint looks down on one of the largest palm groves in Morocco, a green ribbon of date palms and gardens below the town. Just beyond, the Todra Gorge narrows to a corridor of rock walls up to 300 m high above a clear stream. The walk along the riverbed is flat and easy, about 45 minutes to an hour, and in summer the water is pleasant for paddling.

After lunch, cross the stony plain via Tinejdad, where lines of wells mark the khettaras, the underground irrigation channels that still feed the oases. In Erfoud, the gateway to the Tafilalet, visit a fossil workshop where 400-million-year-old marine fossils are cut and polished into tables, bowls and souvenirs. You spend the night in Erfoud, so tomorrow you reach the dunes rested.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
08:30 – Breakfast and departure.
09:30 – Tinghir palm grove viewpoint.
10:00 – Todra Gorge walk (45 min–1 hour).
13:00 – Lunch (not included).
14:30 – Tinejdad and the khettaras.
16:00 – Erfoud: fossil workshop, check-in.
19:30 – Dinner at your hotel.

FIRST-TIMER TIPS
• Fossils are sold everywhere; buy from workshops for genuine pieces and keep the receipt.
• The gorge is shaded and cool in the morning, the best time to walk.
• Try madfouna, the stuffed 'Berber pizza', a speciality of the region.

INCLUDED: vehicle and driver, hotel with dinner and breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, tips.

Overnight: Erfoud (hotel)
Meals: breakfast and dinner

What to expect: a camel ride of about 1–1.5 hours, a camp with beds, dinner and drums, and a very starry sky.

A short drive brings you from Erfoud to Merzouga, at the edge of the Erg Chebbi, a sea of orange dunes up to about 150 m high. On the way, stop in Rissani, the old caravan town where the Alaouite dynasty began, to see its busy market and the Mausoleum of Moulay Ali Cherif from outside. The rest of the day is free: rest at a hotel by the dunes, try sandboarding, or book an optional 4x4 tour to the Gnawa musicians of Khamlia and a nomad family's tent.

In the late afternoon, leave your main luggage in the vehicle and meet your camel caravan. The handlers lead the camels on foot into the dunes as the light softens, timed so you can climb a crest and watch the sun set over the Sahara. At the camp you're welcomed with mint tea; dinner is served in a dining tent or outside, often followed by Berber drums around the fire. Away from any town, the night sky is full of stars. Tents have proper beds and blankets; bathrooms are shared or private depending on the level you booked.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
09:00 – Breakfast and short drive to Merzouga via Rissani.
11:00 – Free time or optional 4x4 tour (not included).
13:00 – Lunch (not included).
17:00 – Camel trek into Erg Chebbi.
18:30 – Sunset on the dunes.
19:00 – Camp, mint tea, dinner.

FIRST-TIMER TIPS
• Lean back when the camel stands up and forward when it kneels; hold the handle.
• Pack a small bag for the night: toiletries, charger, a warm layer, a head torch.
• Wear a scarf against wind and sand, and sunglasses.

INCLUDED: vehicle and driver, camel trek, desert camp with dinner and breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: optional 4x4 tour, lunch, tips.

Overnight: Erg Chebbi (desert camp)
Meals: breakfast and dinner

What to expect: sunrise over the dunes, then the longest drive of the trip, about 9–10 hours with regular stops.

Wake before dawn and climb a dune to watch the sun rise over the Sahara, the sand turning from grey to gold. After breakfast at camp, ride or walk back to the edge of the dunes, freshen up at a partner hotel and set off for Marrakech by a different road from the one you came on.

The route runs west through Rissani and across the black stony desert around Alnif and N'Kob, a striking landscape of dark volcanic hills dotted with fossil shops, then joins the Draa side of the Anti-Atlas before reaching Ouarzazate. After a last break, you climb back over the Tizi n'Tichka pass, with the High Atlas glowing in the late-afternoon light, and arrive in Marrakech in the evening. Your driver drops you at your riad, hotel or the airport.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
06:00 – Sunrise on the dunes.
07:30 – Breakfast at camp; return to Merzouga, shower.
08:30 – Departure via Rissani.
11:30 – Alnif / N'Kob: coffee and fossil shops.
13:00 – Lunch (not included).
15:00 – Ouarzazate area: break.
16:30 – Tizi n'Tichka pass.
19:00–19:30 – Arrival in Marrakech.

FIRST-TIMER TIPS
• Keep snacks, water and a charger in the car for the long afternoon.
• Book departing flights for the next day, not this evening.
• Change leftover dirhams back before you fly; they can't be exchanged abroad.

INCLUDED: vehicle and driver, drop-off in Marrakech.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, tips.

Overnight: not included (end of the tour)
Meals: breakfast

faq.question: Is this tour suitable for a first trip to Morocco?
faq.answer: Yes, it was written for first-timers. Each day explains what to expect, includes practical tips (money, tipping, photos, clothing) and has a relaxed pace: short drives on the first days, a night near the dunes before the camel ride, and comfortable rooms or desert tents with real beds every night.

faq.question: How long are the drives?
faq.answer: Days 1 to 4 have 1 to 4 hours of driving each, split by stops at viewpoints, kasbahs and gorges. Day 5, back to Marrakech, is the long one: about 560 km, 9 to 10 hours with regular breaks. The vehicle is air-conditioned and your driver stops whenever you ask.

faq.question: How cold is the desert at night?
faq.answer: From November to March it can drop close to freezing; camps provide thick blankets, but bring a warm layer and a hat. In spring and autumn nights are cool and pleasant. In summer days are very hot (often above 40 °C) and nights are warm.

faq.question: Is the desert camp comfortable?
faq.answer: Yes. Tents have proper beds, blankets and lighting, and dinner is served in a dining tent or outside under the stars. Depending on the level you book, bathrooms are shared or private, with toilets and showers. Your main luggage stays in the vehicle; take a small bag for the night.

faq.question: How much should I tip?
faq.answer: Tipping is customary but always up to you. As a guide, many travellers give the local guide in Ait Ben Haddou around 50–100 dirhams, camel handlers 50–100 dirhams, and their driver around 100–150 dirhams per day at the end of the trip. Your driver can advise on the spot.

faq.question: Is it a private tour?
faq.answer: Yes. Only you and the people you book with travel in the vehicle, with your own driver for the five days. You choose the start date, and the pace and stops adapt to your group. There is no minimum group size.

faq.question: Which meals are included?
faq.answer: Breakfast and dinner every day, at your hotels and in the desert camp. Lunches and drinks are not included, so you can stop wherever you like; your driver knows good local places. Tell us about allergies or dietary needs when you book.

faq.question: What should I pack?
faq.answer: Layers for cold mornings and nights, a scarf for sun and sand, sunglasses, sunscreen, a hat, comfortable walking shoes, a head torch, a reusable water bottle and a small overnight bag for the camp. Modest clothing (shoulders and knees covered) is appreciated in villages.

faq.question: Can I skip the camel ride?
faq.answer: Yes. If you'd rather not ride, or have back or mobility problems, you can reach the camp by 4x4 and still walk up a dune for sunset. The camels walk slowly and are led on foot, so most first-timers, including children, find the ride easy.

faq.question: Do I need to bring cash?
faq.answer: Yes. Cards are rarely accepted outside the cities, so withdraw dirhams in Marrakech before leaving. Plan for lunches, drinks, entrance fees (Taourirt Kasbah, film studios), tips and any souvenirs such as fossils or rose products.

faq.question: Can we start from Marrakech airport?
faq.answer: Yes. If you arrive in the morning, we can pick you up at Marrakech Menara airport and start the tour straight away. At the end, your driver can drop you at the airport, but we recommend flying the next day because Day 5 is long.

faq.question: Is the tour suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children usually love the camels, the dunes and the fossils. The first four days have short drives; the last day is long, so bring games or tablets. Tell us the ages of your children and whether you need child seats.

faq.question: When is the best time for this desert tour?
faq.answer: October to May is the most comfortable. Spring brings the rose harvest in the Valley of Roses (late April–May); autumn has warm days and mild nights. Winter is sunny but cold at night in the mountains and desert, and summer is very hot in the afternoons, so the camel ride is kept for the late afternoon.
